To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
An online interactive psychoeducational website for people at high genetic risk for depression improved intention to adopt or actual adoption of depression prevention strategies.

a website designed to meet the psychoeducational needs of people at familial risk of major depressive disorder was more effective than a control website at improving the intention to, or actual adoption by, participants of depression prevention strategies.
an interactive online intervention improved the knowledge of people with a family member with depression, and their intentions to adopt depression prevention strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of online psychoeducational interventions for people with a first-degree family history of depression and bipolar disorder.
the development and evaluation of a website that is aimed at improving outcomes in people at familial risk of developing depression.

the identification of risk factors for depression in people who have a family history of mood disorders, and the development of interventions that will help people who are at risk of depression to reduce their risk of developing the disorder.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first website that focuses specifically on psychoeducational needs of those at high risk of depression.

the intervention was effective for the primary outcome (intention to adopt or actual adoption of prevention strategies) and secondary outcome measures of knowledge of risk factors and prevention of depression and accurate estimation of risk for bipolar disorder.

the intervention was associated with improved intentions to adopt, and adoption of, depression preventive strategies, improved knowledge of depression risk, and improved estimates of personal risk for developing bipolar disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is the first study to develop and evaluate a psychoeducational online intervention for people at familial-risk for depression.
we have developed and trialled a website that is the first to address the specific informational needs of people at familial risk of mood disorders.
the intervention was effective in improving intention to adopt, and actual adoption of, prevention strategies, and improving knowledge of risk factors and prevention of BD, but not for depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a psychoeducational website can be a useful tool to improve the knowledge and risk perception of people who have a family history of MDD or BD.
an interactive website can be an important adjunct to primary health care for people at familial high risk of depression.
a psychoeducational website can improve the outcomes of individuals with a family history depression.
